activity.notes: Representative chronological point at c.1090 BCE for the Gideon/Jerubbaal tradition. This is not a lifespan, judgeship tenure, or claim of exact campaign dating. Cline uses 1090 BCE as a historical-synthesis anchor for Gideon's Midianite conflict; the late twelfth/early eleventh-century Jerubbaal inscription independently shows the name in roughly the same era but is not treated as identification of Gideon. ATLAS uses one uncertain point instead of the former 1150-1050 BCE 100-year rail.

sources.title: Hebrew Bible — Judges 6–8
sources.citation_text: Primary textual source for Gideon, also called Jerubbaal, and the Midianite conflict tradition.

sources.title: Eric H. Cline, The Battles of Armageddon: Megiddo and the Jezreel Valley from the Bronze Age to the Nuclear Age
sources.citation_text: Cline's historical synthesis treats Gideon's conflict with the Midianites and Amalekites under the chronological heading 1090 BCE. ATLAS uses that date only as an uncertain representative anchor.
sources.locator: Chapter: Gideon, the Midianites, and the Amalekites, 1090 B.C.

sources.title: The Jerubba‘al Inscription from Khirbet al-Ra‘i: a Proto-Canaanite (Early Alphabetic) inscription
sources.citation_text: Rollston, Garfinkel, Keimer, Davis, and Ganor date the Khirbet al-Ra‘i Jerubbaal inscription to the late twelfth or early eleventh century BCE. The inscription supports the period-use of the name only and is not identification of the biblical Gideon.

review_context.chronology_policy: Replace a broad era window with one uncertain representative point when person-specific start/end boundaries are not defensible.
